label: Compares null with = instead of IS NULL
description: The learner writes `WHERE city = NULL` and gets no rows, because null is unknown and never equals anything, including itself.

remediation.explanation: Null is not a value, so `=` cannot match it. The test is `IS NULL` (or `IS NOT NULL`).

label: Confuses the null value with the string 'null'
description: The learner writes `WHERE city = 'NULL'` and expects it to find null values, but that compares against the four-character text 'NULL'.

remediation.explanation: The value NULL is unknown, not text. `'NULL'` is a string of four letters. Only `IS NULL` finds the unknown.

label: Filters on aggregates in WHERE instead of HAVING
description: The learner writes `WHERE COUNT(*) > 1`, but WHERE runs before groups exist. Aggregate conditions belong in HAVING.

remediation.explanation: WHERE filters rows before grouping. HAVING filters groups after aggregation. `HAVING COUNT(*) > 1` is the working form.

label: Treats names or row positions as identity
description: The learner joins, groups, or points at rows using a person's name, some display text, or line position instead of a key.

remediation.explanation: Names repeat and positions shift on every sort. Only a primary key identifies a row; group by the key and carry the name as a label.

label: Trusts counts inflated by join fan-out
description: The learner joins customers to orders, sees COUNT(*) return 5, and reports 5 customers, when 3 orders belong to one customer.

remediation.explanation: A one-to-many join repeats the one side. COUNT(*) counts joined rows; COUNT(DISTINCT key) counts entities. Predict the row count before you aggregate.

label: Uses DISTINCT to hide a fan-out
description: The learner slaps DISTINCT on a doubled result. The duplicate rows vanish, but any totals stay wrong.

remediation.explanation: DISTINCT removes duplicate output rows; it does not repair a doubled SUM. Fix the grain: aggregate to one row per entity, then join.

label: Omits the ON condition and pairs every row with every row
description: The learner writes a join without ON, or assumes SQLite will guess the relationship, and gets every left row paired with every right row.

remediation.explanation: Without a condition the join is a cartesian product: 3 customers x 5 orders is 15 rows. State the relationship: `ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id`.

label: Writes SELECT * by default
description: The learner selects every column for every query, shipping extra data and breaking silently when the schema changes.

remediation.explanation: Name the columns the question needs. `SELECT status, total_cents FROM orders` says what the report is about and survives schema changes.

label: Assumes ORDER BY sorts largest first and clause details can shuffle
description: The learner writes ORDER BY total_cents and expects biggest-first, or rearranges LIMIT and ORDER BY as if order did not matter.

remediation.explanation: ORDER BY sorts ascending by default; biggest-first needs DESC. Clauses run in a fixed order: SELECT, FROM, WHERE, ORDER BY, LIMIT.

label: Runs UPDATE or DELETE without a WHERE clause
description: The learner writes `UPDATE orders SET status = 'shipped'` with no WHERE and changes every row in the table.

remediation.explanation: An UPDATE or DELETE without WHERE touches every row. Preview first with a SELECT using the same WHERE, then run the change inside a transaction.

label: Believes changes are undoable without a transaction
description: The learner assumes SQLite keeps an undo history or that ROLLBACK works after an autocommitted statement.

remediation.explanation: Each statement outside a transaction commits instantly. Only work inside BEGIN ... ROLLBACK can be undone, and only before COMMIT.

label: Adds an index to every column
description: The learner treats indexes as free speed and indexes every column, slowing every insert and update.

remediation.explanation: Every index must be maintained on every write. Index the columns your frequent queries filter and join on, then confirm the plan uses them.

label: Reads a full table scan as proof the index is broken
description: The learner sees SCAN in EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN and concludes the index failed, when the planner simply chose the cheapest plan for the data size.

remediation.explanation: Reading 5 rows is cheaper than walking an index and fetching each row. SCAN is the right plan for small tables; SEARCH USING INDEX appears when the data is big enough to matter.

label: Keeps repeating groups in one table
description: The learner stores several things in one cell, like 'Espresso Blend, Ceramic Mug', or widens the table with product1, product2, product3 columns.

remediation.explanation: One kind of thing per table, one fact per cell. Move the repeating items to their own table and link with a foreign key.
